title: Postmortem: embeddings/rerank GPU memory leak caused capacity drop and fallback quality regression
creator: Maya Chen
summary: During a rolling rollout of a CPU-to-GPU optimized embedding runtime, one of the new JNI-based GPU drivers leaked device memory in the rerank worker process. Over ~3 hours this led to progressive GPU OOMs and autoscaler thrashing, triggering an emergency fallback to a lower-precision model variant which caused measurable quality regressions for reranking results. Service capacity dropped 45% at peak and tail latency spiked beyond SLOs.
impact: ~45% capacity reduction for rerank endpoints in us-west-2 for 3.5 hours; increased 95th percentile latency from 220ms to 1.4s; ~12% degradation in rerank MRR on monitored query set while fallback model was active; several enterprise customers observed degraded relevance in production queries.
detection: On-call paging via SLO alerting (high 95p latency) followed by customer complaint flagged to support. Alert correlated with a rising GPU memory usage signal from the job-level dashboard (gpu_mem_used_bytes per process).
timeline: 2026-02-26 03:12 UTC - SLO alert fires for rerank-95p latency; 03:18 UTC - On-call (Ravi) joins incident channel; 03:30 UTC - Observed burst in gpu_mem_used_bytes for rerank-worker-3; 03:45 UTC - Autoscaler attempted scale-up but new pods also experienced rapid GPU OOMs; 04:05 UTC - Emergency traffic routing policy activated to divert traffic to lower-tier region and enable fallback model variant; 04:22 UTC - Fallback to float16-quant model completed; 04:30-06:40 UTC - Service recovered some throughput but quality regression detected in eval harness; 06:45 UTC - Hotfix (revert JNI driver artifact) deployed to canary and validated; 07:10 UTC - Gradual rollforward of fixed runtime to all nodes; 07:55 UTC - Incident declared resolved after 2 stable hours of SLO compliance.
root_cause: A memory leak in a new JNI binding that manages device-side buffers for the GPU-optimized embedding kernel. The leak only manifested under the rerank access pattern (many short-lived requests with varying sequence lengths). The autoscaler lacked a protection policy for repeated OOMs on scale-up that caused thrashing and delayed recovery. Additionally, the rollout did not include a model-output-quality guard that would have prevented automatic fallback without triggering manual review.
mitigations: 1) Immediate: Activated traffic routing to reduce load on affected cluster and enabled fallback model variant to preserve availability. 2) Hotfix: Reverted the JNI binding in the runtime package (PR #rfr/4231) and redeployed. 3) Short-term: Added an autoscaler circuit-breaker to stop scale-ups after N consecutive OOMs for a job and route traffic to healthy pools.
long_term_actions: - Root fix: Replace JNI memory management with a safe RAII-style allocator and add unit tests that simulate the rerank short-lived allocation pattern (owner: infra-runtime, ETA: 2026-03-12). - Observability: Add per-process cumulative device-allocation counter and alert when growth rate exceeds threshold (owner: observability, ETA: 2026-03-08). - Rollout policy: Require canary run with production-like short-sequence synthetic workload and verification of memory stability before widening (owner: release, ETA: 2026-03-05). - Quality guard: Add an automated A/B quality monitor that blocks fallback rollouts if rerank MRR drops >5% on golden set (owner: evals, ETA: 2026-03-19). - Autoscaler: Implement backoff policy for repeated OOMs and an operator-visible suppression flag (owner: autoscale, ETA: 2026-04-02).
rollback_decision: Reverted JNI artifact to last stable version. Decision rationale: revert minimized customer impact quickly and validated that the driver was the root cause in canary. A patch-based fix required additional validation and would have prolonged impact window.
metrics: - Peak capacity loss: 45% (measured by provisioned tokens/sec) - Rerank 95p latency: baseline 220ms -> incident 1.4s - Rerank MRR on golden queries: baseline 0.321 -> during fallback 0.283 (-12%) - Number of OOMs observed: 78 across 12 nodes
action_items: Implement JNI RAII allocator and unit tests (infra-runtime) - due 2026-03-12
Add per-process device allocation metric and alert (observability) - due 2026-03-08
Add canary workload for short-sequence embedding pattern to rollout checklist (release) - due 2026-03-05
Autoscaler backoff for repeated OOMs and suppression flag (autoscale) - due 2026-04-02
Create A/B quality gate to prevent silent fallback on rerank (evals) - due 2026-03-19
Customer outreach: notify impacted customers with summary + remediation steps (success) - due 2026-03-06
post_incident_notes: We observed that the rerank workload's allocation churn uniquely exposed a JNI lifecycle bug that wasn't caught by prior GPU-heavy synthetic canaries. The combination of a binary runtime change + autoscaler behavior caused availability to degrade faster than expected. Future rollouts will use more diverse canaries, stricter autoscaler safety, and automatic quality gates to prevent silent fallbacks.
